source: Create a detailed Titanic-inspired ocean liner hull for a showcase. Make the ship very long and proportionally accurate, with a pointed bow, rounded stern, black lower hull, red underwater hull, and white upper hull. Use separate Parts/Models for major sections so I can edit them later. Do not create the interior yet.

image_prompt.text: The ocean liner hull as the hero build: very long and proportionally accurate, pointed bow, rounded stern, black lower hull above the waterline, red underwater hull below it, white upper hull on top, composed to be framed from vantage points along the quay
Visitor arrival placed and oriented so the first view is a composed three-quarter shot of the bow, never the unbuilt interior or the open section seams
Secondary composed viewpoints distinct from the hero shot - alongside the red boot-topping at the waterline and astern of the rounded counter

layout_placement.text: Spawn point set at the composed first-reveal vantage on the bow side

notes: The prompt asks for major sections as separate Parts/Models so they stay editable; the layout handoff has no field for output part hierarchy, so it is recorded here.
Explicitly no interior this pass - do not route P3 even though a liner would normally imply enterable decks.
Hull length at Titanic proportions is roughly 900 studs, which sits in the district band and is long for a single top-down frame; a side elevation may serve this build better than a plan view.

open_questions.ask: How long should the hull be in studs? Titanic proportions come out around 900 studs, which is a wide frame for one image.
Do players walk the decks of this showcase, or is the ship an object to be viewed from outside only?

theme: Realistic period maritime (1910s ocean liner livery)

coverage_missing.ask: How long should the hull be in studs?
Is this a walkable showcase or a static model to look at?
Period-accurate 1912 livery, or a stylised Roblox-friendly version of it?

answers.ask: How long should the hull be in studs? Titanic proportions come out around 900 studs, which is a wide frame for one image.
answers.answer: Use a smaller but still very long showcase scale of about 500 studs overall, preserving Titanic-like proportions.

answers.ask: Do players walk the decks of this showcase, or is the ship an object to be viewed from outside only?
answers.answer: This is an exterior showcase object viewed from outside only; do not build playable deck access or an interior yet.
